programmes.d: Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.
When a dedicated, well-respected teacher disappeared, police had to determine if she'd gone on vacation without telling anyone or if she was the victim of foul play.
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her.

When a 9-year-old girl goes missing, police and volunteers spend weeks searching for her. A psychic's vision leads to a field where her body is discovered, along with what investigators hope is enough evidence to find her killer.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement.

This killer probably hoped to cover his tracks by staging the crime scene. But investigators saw through the attempt almost immediately and turned to forensic science to learn what really happened that night.
The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.

In 1984, California firefighters battled ten arson fires in three weeks. When cigarettes and a scrap of paper connected the case to similar fires further north, the hunt was on for a dangerous pyromaniac.
A jeweler's search through old sales records helps police find likely suspects in a couple's murder.

A young man was killed in a mysterious car crash, but the evidence at the scene led investigators to believe it was not an accident. Forensic science revealed what really happened and the truth devastated three families.
Garbage bag leads to a killer.
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her. But investigators soon poked holes in his story, leaving the case unsolved for 14 years.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body.
After the 1996 murder of Seattle residents Raquel Rivera and Jay Johnson, evidence from the couple's dog eventually ties one of the murderers to the scene.
The sensitive nose of a forensic examiner sniffs out murder.

A healthy young man dies mysteriously in his sleep and toxicology tests reveal a lethal dose of lidocaine in his blood. Investigators find a suicide note and presume he killed himself until a forensic linguist examines the note.
An assailant avoids the law for 16 years due to a lack of evidence.

After a day of fishing in a quiet village in Switzerland, a teenage boy doesn't return home as planned. The investigation reveals some important microscopic evidence in the water near where he was last seen.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun.

When heart surgeon Darryl Sutorius is found dead in the basement of his upscale Cincinnati home, police assume he committed suicide. Further investigation reveals that his new wife Della has a history of violence and an insatiable desire for money.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause the deaths of three people.

While vacationing in California, Earl Morris learns that his wife has gone missing from their Arizona home. The search for Ruby Morris involves dozens of investigators and scientists — and even the Coast Guard.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.

Two men are murdered while sleeping in their beds. The next night, arson destroys a family planning clinic. Investigators wonder whether some shards of glass, paint chips and a chicken feather could link what appear to be two separate crimes.
Using an anonymous letter and geographical profiling, investigators close in on a serial rapist.
In 2004, Rebecca Barney and her soon-to-be ex-husband Fred were found shot to death in their Tulsa, Oklahoma, home, which had been set on fire.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers.
In 1995, Palm Beach waitress Denise O'Neill is abducted and murdered. Her neighbor Luis Caballero arouses suspicions by behaving oddly toward TV crews covering the crime.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica.

When police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife, authorities linked 20 cat hairs found on her jacket to a cat owned by Beamish's parents. It was the first time animal DNA was used to solve a criminal case.
An examination of the 2002 DC area shooting spree that resulted in ten murders.
A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial.

In 2006, Nevada politician Kathy Augustine died mysteriously during a re-election campaign. The medical examiner could neither isolate the cause of death, nor explain the tiny puncture wounds discovered during the autopsy.
Notepad points to kidnapper.
The victim had been stabbed more than thirty times and the crime scene was awash with her blood. Near her head, police discovered a distinctive button with strands of thread still attached.
Debate over cause of death.

In 1993, the state of Florida was known for more than just Disney World. Worldwide attention focused on a rash of robberies which targeted tourists. Some vacationers were killed in these attacks, but some fought and survived.
A killer leaves the scene with the genetic fingerprint of his victim.

Women in a Louisiana city live in fear of a rapist who leaves no clues to his identity. But technology and behavioral science combine to give police a new forensic tool. Police narrow their search to one man: local policeman Randy Comeaux.
A vacuum-cleaner bag of microscopic paint-particles helps to identify a killer.

A suspect's former lover comes forward with a fantastic tale of murder, mutilation and cremation. But there's no way to test the story's validity — until a plant pathologist and a dendrochronologist conduct tests where the cremation supposedly occurred.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later.
In 1993, 82-year-old Kathryn Bishop was found dead in her Pennsylvania home. Tiny clues on the victim's body would tell police what happened that night.
A physics professor and NASA technology help to catch a killer.
When Rosemary Anderson is found dead on the side of the road, her boyfriend becomes the prime suspect. He eventually confessed to her murder, but so did another man: serial killer Eric Edgar Cooke.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on robberies which targeted tourists in Florida.
Timothy Wilson Spencer was identified as the man who raped and strangled five young women in Virginia. With the use of DNA profiling, an innocent man is freed and the real killer is convicted.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe-print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints.
Police get a clue about a couple who disappeared on Memorial Day weekend during an in-progress robbery. The evidence found solves a brutal crime.
A death in Pennsylvania is strikingly similar to one in North Carolina.

Residents of Noel, Missouri were stunned to learn that their bank had been robbed and the bank president was missing. His body was later found floating in a lake, securely bound to a chair with duct tape.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.

Firefighters find an entire family dead inside their home in an apparent murder-suicide, but there are several inconsistent clues in the rubble. Could ballistics, a time card and some secret audiotapes unravel the mystery?
A pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom.

In 2007, the Florida mobile home of Effie and Michael Ratley catches fire. Michael heroically rescues his wife and infant son. A month later, his wife is found beaten to death in a bedroom of his parents' home.
Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a murder crime scene.
It's usually easy to determine how a criminal entered the crime scene. But in this case, it looked as if the killer vanished into thin air — and perhaps he had.
A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has an almost perfect alibi.

A brilliant young architect falls ill and dies just before she is to testify in a criminal trial. The autopsy reveals she'd been poisoned with arsenic. Investigators must determine who had a motive for murder.
A union official is executed in his home not long after a strike by the union membership.

Three seemingly unrelated deaths prove to be serial murders. The killer had been careful; he used poison which had no taste or odor. Fortunately for investigators, it also had a unique chemical signature.
In 1988, the body of a young woman was discovered in an Ohio river.
Crystal Faye Todd's case is examined; the popular high school student was raped and murdered.
When more than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984, investigators uncovered a secret plot to influence local elections.
Police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife.
Two different men called police to report the same murder. Apparently, neither one knew that the other had called. The investigation uncovered even more unusual circumstances.
More than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984.
When a successful stockbroker doesn't return home after a late shift, his wife reports him missing.
A woman is found dead from a gunshot wound and police suspect her husband.

A fire erupts in Kings Cross Station in London, killing 31 people and injuring dozens more. Investigators pinpoint the cause of the fire, but it takes state-of-the-art technology and fluid dynamics experts to explain why it became a deadly inferno.
In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with $500,000 in gold coins.
The victim had ingested a massive amount of cyanide. An unlikely clue — a flaw on a mailing envelope — exposed a murderer who was willing to kill innocent people.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
The prime suspect had a criminal record and his driver's license was found at the scene of a brutal double homicide.
In 1984, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box.

A mysterious computer crash pushed a thriving manufacturing company to the brink of collapse, jeopardizing hundreds of employees' jobs. Forensic investigators must determine if the crash was the result of a computer defect, human error or sabotage.
A victim's knowledge of forensic evidence leads police to her abductor.

Soon after organizing a workers' strike, a union official is executed in his home. Neither his wife nor anyone in the neighborhood hear any gunshots. It takes a forensic sound test, an electron microscope and a nightgown to explain why.
The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage.

The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage. Conventional means of identifying the victim are impossible, leading investigators to rely on DNA, forensic anthropology and toxicology.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.
Faced with three homicides that appear to be professional executions, investigators on both sides of the Atlantic must find a common thread between the victims.
Forensic developments reveal new facts in the case of a man convicted of sexual assault.

In 2002, a small community in upstate New York was devastated when Patty Wlasiuk died in a truck accident. But burdock seed pods found in her hair and on her clothes indicated that this was no accident — it was cold-blooded murder.
The murder of a couple puzzles investigators until the victims' dog leads police to the killer.
Authorities track a kidnapper who let his victim write a last will and informed the family of her murder. A phone number written on a previous page left a lasting impression, which helped to convict.
Soon after becoming pregnant, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates.
In 1999, Patrick McRae was found dead in his Des Moines home and the crime scene was awash with blood. Analysis showed it had come from two people, one of whom was female.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas.

The investigation into the kidnapping and rape of an 18-year-old Ohio woman is aided when the victim returns hours after the incident occurred. With her help, the police are able to track the assailant to his front door.
An abandoned, still-running car leads investigators to a body with unusual marks.
In 1999, a 12-year-old was found murdered in her Minnesota home. Despite a meticulous search of the home and an exhaustive investigation, police had no suspects.
Police uncover deleted computer files during an investigation.

In 1996, police received a call from Darlie Routier telling them of her two sons' murders. The police found the killer by analyzing blood spatter, doing behavioral profiling and analyzing Darlie's 911 call.
A suspicious neighbor gives police a break in a cold case.

A 19-year-old woman was found dead in her car; the scene had been staged to make murder appear to be suicide. During their investigation, police discovered the victim was involved in a love quadrangle, giving several people a motive to kill her.
The 1987 disappearance of Houston resident Tracy Jo Shine is recalled.

When Scott Dunn goes missing, police spray his bedroom with Luminol and uncover a scene of horrific violence. Now investigators face a daunting task: proving that Scott Dunn had been murdered without a body, a witness or a murder weapon.
Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.
